newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE PESO DIPS IN CAUTIOUS MARKET.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE PESO DIPS IN CAUTIOUS MARKET.

text.p: The Philippine peso dipped at the close of trading on Friday as banks took a cautious stance ahead of the expected return of foreign banks in the spot market, traders said.
"The market was sideways. There's uncertainty when foreign funds do return to the market. There's no price liquidity without them," a trader said.
The peso closed at 28.51 from 28.46. Trading was in a narrow range of 28.45/28.55. Volume was thin at $22.5 million from $58.5 million.
The Bankers Association of the Philippines had recommended to its board the return of foreign banks to the Philippine Dealing System (PDS) because of the relative stability in the peso.
Foreign banks were excluded two weeks ago from the PDS to ease the pressure on the peso after it was effectively devalued on July 11.
"We want to know whether the foreign banks would be buying or selling," a trader said.
Traders said the central bank was not in the market but it quoted bid and offer rates for the dollar at 27/28.70.
On Thursday, traders said the central bank bought $35 million at 28.37 for delivery on Monday.
